summary: Enragée Point light on Chéticamp Island, first lit here in 1937 after a move from the island's south-west end; a fire in 1956 led to the present concrete tower, last kept by a keeper until 1988.

structures.note: Parks Canada ties the concrete tower to the 1956 fire; the Lighthouse Directory dates it 1957
Lighthouse at Enragée Point from 1937, destroyed by fire 19 October 1956 (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Route: Cabot Trail, then Cheticamp Island Road and Lighthouse Road, about 6 km.

events.note: Predecessor light completed on the south-west end of Cheticamp Island, first exhibited 23 July 1872 (not this point)
Stays attached to the island light after it vibrated in winter gales (predecessor light)
Lightning struck the island light and caused considerable damage; the illuminating apparatus was not injured
New tower, 19 ft square at the base and 25 ft high, built beside the dwelling on the island; iron lantern moved to it
Primary light moved from the south-west point of Cheticamp Island to Enragée Point; first light at this site
Fire destroyed the wooden lighthouse on 19 October 1956
Concrete octagon replaced it; Parks Canada ties the tower to the 1956 fire, the Lighthouse Directory dates it 1957
Made a three-person station; electrified December 1967; 400-watt mercury-vapour lamp and an electronic horn
Staff reduced to two keepers; one keeper by the end of the decade
Last keeper, Gregoire Patrick LeFort, retired 1 April 1988
Designated a heritage lighthouse under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act; announced 22 August 2019 (LighthouseFriends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Parks Canada says the concrete tower replaced the wooden light after a fire in 1956; the Lighthouse Directory gives 1957 for the tower. The story gives 1956 and notes the directory's 1957.
The 1872 light was on the south-west end of Cheticamp Island, not at Enragée Point. The first light at this site is 1937, as Parks Canada and LighthouseFriends both give it.

notes_for_editor: The keeper list is LighthouseFriends' list for the 1872 island light through to 1988, which the page treats as one station; this roster keeps the 1872-1937 keepers because LighthouseFriends prints them on this page, and the story says so. The record's first_lit 1937 refers to Enragée Point only. 'P. Robin & Co.' and 'Charles Robin & Co.' are printed as firm names; no individual is identified. The 1903 keepers' list was read as OCR and 'Muise, Marcellin' is matched to Cheticamp by row (scan 231, printed 218, 1904v38i8p21_0209, the same page as Cape George); the page image was viewed at screen resolution and the Muise row was not magnified, so the row match rests mainly on the OCR line order. The story's sentence about the island light's 1882 stays and 1883 lightning now says it was the island light, not Enragee Point. The 1915 Department table was checked for this station and not used. The Kinburn wreck of 1936 rests on Argonauta (quoting Chiasson's book) and on Parks Canada's statement; no newspaper or Coast Guard report was read. Mills, cited in Argonauta, is the 'retired' source. The corpus ends in the 1920s, so 1937 to 1988 staffing rests on LighthouseFriends alone. The Canada.ca 2019 release was not fetched; the designation date comes from LighthouseFriends. Parks and Rowlett disagree on the tower year (1956 against 1957).
